dedupe_keys.name: fapri mu agricultural market models and baseline outlook university of missouri

description: FAPRI-MU maintains economic models of key agricultural commodity markets that estimate how policy options and market conditions affect prices, quantities, producers, consumers and government costs for crops, livestock and biofuels. Its main output is an annual baseline, a ten-year projection of US agricultural markets, farm program spending and farm income published each spring, with baseline updates later in the year and stochastic analysis that runs the models many times under different yield shocks and petroleum price swings. It is produced by the Food and Agricultural Policy Research Institute at the University of Missouri, active since 1984, working with collaborators at the University of Nevada, Reno, Texas A&M, Arkansas and Texas Tech on international crops, farm-level impacts, rice and cotton. Coverage is the United States with international links. The 2026 outlook, report 01-26 of 26 March 2026, is a free PDF with Excel tables of historical and projected data; the models themselves are not distributed. Caveats: baselines assume current policy and normal weather, and the page gives no licence. For simulation it supplies projected crop and biofuel market conditions and yield-shock responses for studies of agricultural resilience and of freight, storage and energy demand. It is related to the IMAGE record in this catalogue, a global model of land use and climate.
